2. Facts necessary for disposal of this appeal are that the appellant as the pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 1997 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Harirampur, Manikganj under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for pre-emption of the case land stating, inter alia, that he was a co-sharer by inheritance in the case holding. Opposite party Nos.3-5(in the miscellaneous case) respondent Nos. 3-5 herein (hereinafter referred to as the transferors) transferred the case land to pre-emptee Nos. 1 and 2 by a registered kabala dated 22.05.1997  for a consideration of taka 30,000.00 only without issuing any notice to him under section 89 of the Act, 1950. 

 6. From the order of the trial Court, it appears that it rejected the preemption application on the clear finding that the transfer in question was a mortgage and not an out and out sale within the meaning section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (the Act, 1950) and therefore, it was not pre-emptable. In coming to the said finding, the trial Court considered the evidence of the PWs and the DWs and came to the further finding that the ekrarnama was executed by the pre-emptees on the same date of the registration of the sale deed. In treating the sale deed as a kot kabala, the trial court considered the following facts: 

 8. The High Court Division considered the provisions of section 95A of the Act, 1950, and gave the finding that "On close scrutiny of the provision of section 95A, it appears that if there be a deed for out and out sale with an agreement for reconveyance executed simultaneously on the same date and those two together will constitute a complete usufractuary mortgage. So, the usufractualy mortgage as contemplated under section 95(1)(2) of the said Act is completely different one. By the deeming clause of section 95A of the said Act, it should be treated as a complete usufractuary mortage where there is a deed for out and out sale with an agreement for reconveyance." and on consideration of the fact that in the instant case, there was an agreement for re-conveyance of the land transferred by the kabala under preemption executed on the same date by the pre-emptees, held that the same was not an out and sale deed, but a kot kabala and as such, that was not pre-emptably and accordingly rejected the preemption application. The High Court Division also held that in a case with "an agreement for re-conveyance with a deed of out sale as contemplated under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not required to be compulsorily registered as is required under section 95(2) of the Act."
